all.title: All signals
all.reason: These routes are not the full DFDS network. They are the routes where this dashboard currently has public signals.
all.risk: App friction, disruption communication, and unclear journey expectations.
all.action: Prioritize app reliability, route-specific messaging, and disruption communication.

dover-calais.title: Dover-Calais
dover-calais.reason: Selected because public reporting and Reddit discussion surfaced delay, border-control, and ticket-rule signals.
dover-calais.action: Clarify delay guidance, border-control timing, and ticket conditions before purchase.

newhaven-dieppe.title: Newhaven-Dieppe
newhaven-dieppe.reason: Selected because public reporting mentioned passenger compensation after an onboard incident.
newhaven-dieppe.risk: Weak disruption recovery can become a brand story.
newhaven-dieppe.action: Create a route-specific incident recovery and compensation communication playbook.

newcastle-ijmuiden.title: Newcastle-IJmuiden
newcastle-ijmuiden.reason: Selected because a recent Apple App Store review mentions mobile check-in being unavailable on this route.
newcastle-ijmuiden.risk: Customers may expect app features that do not exist on their route.
newcastle-ijmuiden.action: Show route-level app feature availability before customers rely on mobile check-in.

jersey.title: Jersey / Channel Islands
jersey.reason: Selected because public coverage surfaced Jersey service-level and freight-pricing concerns.
jersey.risk: A local service issue can be hidden by the all-company average.
jersey.action: Track Jersey separately and report service confidence as its own market lens.

appReviewEvidence.title: Account handoff failure
appReviewEvidence.evidence: The review says the app redirects to DFDS.com and then does not accept account credentials.
appReviewEvidence.businessMeaning: Customers trying to manage travel digitally may lose trust before they reach the ferry experience.

appReviewEvidence.title: Route feature gap
appReviewEvidence.evidence: The reviewer says mobile check-in was unavailable for the Newcastle to IJmuiden route.
appReviewEvidence.businessMeaning: Feature availability needs route-level messaging so customers do not expect unsupported digital services.

appReviewEvidence.title: Booking retrieval failure
appReviewEvidence.evidence: The reviewer says a booking disappeared and re-adding it returned an unauthorized-access message.
appReviewEvidence.businessMeaning: Booking visibility is a high-stakes digital trust issue because it affects travel confidence.

appReviewEvidence.title: Useful when it works
appReviewEvidence.evidence: A positive review describes the app as handy for travel.
appReviewEvidence.businessMeaning: The app has a clear customer value proposition if reliability problems are reduced.

appReviewEvidence.title: Repeated login loop
appReviewEvidence.evidence: The reviewer describes repeated login loops despite valid credentials and reinstall attempts.
appReviewEvidence.businessMeaning: Authentication issues can convert an otherwise useful travel app into a support burden.

rootCauses.title: Delay recovery and disruption handling
rootCauses.summary: Recent public signals repeatedly mention long delays, disputed compensation, unclear refund handling, and communication gaps during disruption.

rootCauses.title: Onboard experience inconsistency
rootCauses.summary: Trustpilot review themes include staff and service as positives, while cabins, food quality, and boarding experience appear as recurring negatives.

rootCauses.title: Route-specific trust risk in Jersey services
rootCauses.summary: Public coverage around Jersey and Channel Islands ferry services shows concerns about service quality, freight pricing, disruption, and market expectations.

rootCauses.title: Passenger app authentication and booking access
rootCauses.summary: Apple App Store evidence and Google Play rating details show the DFDS Passenger app is a lower-rated channel, with recent complaints around login, booking visibility, account handoff, and mobile check-in expectations.

signals.theme: Overall brand perception is strong but uneven
signals.evidence: DFDS holds a 4.2/5 Trustpilot score from 20,646 reviews, with 53% 5-star and 9% 1-star ratings.
signals.businessMeaning: DFDS has enough public goodwill to protect, but negative experiences are visible and specific enough to influence route-level choice.

signals.theme: Staff and service are brand strengths
signals.evidence: Trustpilot's review summary highlights positive themes around service, friendly staff, comfort, and overall satisfaction.
signals.businessMeaning: Marketing can credibly lean into human service quality if operational weak spots are not ignored.

signals.theme: Boarding, cabins, and food are friction points
signals.evidence: Trustpilot's negative review summary highlights issues with cabins, food quality, customer service, disembarkation, border control, and delays.
signals.businessMeaning: These are not abstract complaints; they map directly to journey moments that shape repeat purchase and recommendation.

signals.evidence: Public reporting described Newhaven-Dieppe passengers seeking compensation after an onboard incident and disrupted journey experience.
signals.businessMeaning: DFDS should treat unusual disruption handling as a brand-protection issue, not only an operations issue.

signals.evidence: BBC reporting around Dover delays includes DFDS advice for passengers to allow extra time because of passport control queues.
signals.businessMeaning: Delay messaging needs to be proactive, route-specific, and framed as customer protection.

signals.theme: Terminal experience is a marketing proof point
signals.evidence: Public Google location profiles show DFDS Calais at 4.2/5 from 2,331 reviews and DFDS Dover at 4.3/5 from 47 reviews.
signals.businessMeaning: Dover-Calais messaging can use terminal efficiency and staff service as proof points, while still addressing signage and food-value friction.

signals.evidence: Public reporting has covered Jersey concerns around DFDS ferry service levels, freight prices, and service disruption.
signals.businessMeaning: Jersey should be monitored as a distinct market perception risk rather than blended into all-DFDS averages.

signals.theme: Crossing experience is stronger than terminal impression
signals.evidence: The Newhaven DFDS Transmanche Google location profile shows 4.2/5 from 478 reviews, with positive signals around booking, check-in, onboard food, crossing comfort, and staff service.
signals.businessMeaning: Marketing can highlight the crossing and onboard experience, while terminal-condition concerns should be treated as a journey-expectation gap.

signals.theme: Mini-cruise and onboard service are strong positives
signals.evidence: The DFDS Newcastle Google location profile shows 4.4/5 from 346 reviews, with positive signals around customer service, cabins, entertainment, family/pet facilities, and mini-cruise experience.
signals.businessMeaning: Newcastle-IJmuiden marketing should lean into onboard experience, service quality, and short-break value.

signals.theme: Passenger app login and booking access are visible pain points
signals.evidence: Recent Apple GB reviews mention failed account credentials, disappeared bookings, unauthorized-access messages, and login loops.
signals.businessMeaning: App problems can reduce customer confidence before the trip even starts.

signals.evidence: A recent Apple review says mobile check-in was not available for Newcastle to IJmuiden.
signals.businessMeaning: Route-specific digital feature availability should be explicit before customers download or rely on the app.

signals.theme: Android app perception is weaker than brand perception
signals.evidence: The Google Play GB page for DFDS - Passenger shows 2.5/5 from 64 reviews.
signals.businessMeaning: The Android channel should be treated as its own customer-experience risk, not hidden inside general brand sentiment.

signals.evidence: A recent Reddit travel thread asks what happens if a DFDS Short Break return ticket is used only one way because it is cheaper than a one-way fare.
signals.businessMeaning: Pricing and ticket-condition messaging may be creating confusion or arbitrage behavior before purchase.

signals.theme: Ferry choice competes with faster transport alternatives
signals.evidence: Reddit travel discussions compare DFDS-style ferry journeys with flying, train, bus, Eurotunnel, and competitor ferry options.
signals.businessMeaning: Marketing should position the ferry around comfort, flexibility, vehicle access, and experience rather than speed alone.

voiceThemes.routeLabel: All routes; strongest signal on Newcastle-IJmuiden
voiceThemes.customerMeaning: Some customers struggle before the trip starts because login, booking retrieval, and route feature availability are unclear.
voiceThemes.marketingAction: Be cautious about promoting mobile self-service until login, booking visibility, and route feature messaging improve.
evidence: Google Play GB shows DFDS - Passenger at 2.5/5 from 64 reviews.
Apple GB App Store shows 3.3/5 from 10 ratings.
Recent Apple reviews mention login loops, missing bookings, and mobile check-in not available on Newcastle-IJmuiden.

voiceThemes.customerMeaning: Location-level Google Reviews show useful strengths around terminal service, boarding flow, staff, and crossing experience.
voiceThemes.marketingAction: Use terminal efficiency, staff service, and route-specific location strengths as proof points in campaign copy.

voiceThemes.customerMeaning: Delays, compensation, border-control queues, and recovery handling can quickly become brand trust issues.
voiceThemes.marketingAction: Prepare clearer disruption messaging before, during, and after travel so customers feel guided rather than surprised.
evidence: Trustpilot negative themes include delays and customer service friction.
BBC reporting surfaced Dover delay and passport-control queue pressure.
Guardian reporting surfaced Newhaven-Dieppe compensation concerns after an onboard incident.

voiceThemes.customerMeaning: Staff friendliness, onboard support, and service quality appear as positive brand assets.
voiceThemes.marketingAction: Use people-led service quality as a brand strength, especially when paired with honest route and disruption messaging.
evidence: Trustpilot summary highlights service, friendly staff, comfort, and satisfaction.
Google location profiles for Dover-Calais, Newhaven, and Newcastle include positive service signals.

voiceThemes.customerMeaning: Jersey-related service and freight-pricing concerns are market-specific and should not be hidden inside DFDS averages.
voiceThemes.marketingAction: Track Channel Islands separately and avoid using all-company performance as a proxy for local confidence.
evidence: Public reporting surfaced Jersey ferry service-level concerns.
Public reporting also surfaced freight-pricing and disruption concerns.

voiceThemes.customerMeaning: Some customers compare ferry options against price rules, one-way fares, Eurotunnel, flights, and other alternatives.
voiceThemes.marketingAction: Make fare rules and value propositions easier to understand before purchase.
evidence: A Reddit travel thread asks about using a DFDS Short Break return ticket one way because it is cheaper than a one-way fare.
Reddit discussions compare ferry travel with flying, train, bus, Eurotunnel, and competitor ferry options.

competitorScope.title: Competitor scope
bullets: 12 ferry brands are included in this comparison view: DFDS plus 11 potential competitors.
The comparison focuses on passenger ferry customers, not DFDS freight or logistics customers.
The first priority is direct route competition, especially Dover-Calais and Channel Islands services.
The second priority is nearby regional competition in the UK-Europe, Nordic, and Baltic ferry markets.
A company is included when customers may compare it with DFDS by route, geography, passenger segment, or travel purpose.
Previous score gaps have been filled with public Trustpilot search-result evidence. These competitor snapshots should be refreshed regularly.

supervisorLogs.module: IT Data Flow and Platform Memory Architecture
supervisorLogs.change: Added a dedicated IT Data Flow page and platform-wide short / medium / long-term memory structure
supervisorLogs.reason: The user wanted a technical view next to Data Basis, plus a shared memory architecture that Mia and the rest of the platform can reuse.
supervisorLogs.scope: IT Data Flow route, Data Basis technical link, dashboard context, local knowledge base, project memories, update logs, daily logs, and UI styling
supervisorLogs.result: The platform now treats IT Data Flow as a separate operational page, exposes a shared memory model across the whole product, and gives Mia access to the new flow and memory context.

supervisorLogs.change: Corrected the rendered proportions in Google Reviews by ferry location
supervisorLogs.reason: The location metric row selector also applied its grid layout to nested progress tracks, so rating fills such as 84% rendered at only about one third of the full track.
supervisorLogs.scope: Overview Google location rating and review-volume bars, responsive CSS, regression test, production dist
supervisorLogs.result: Progress fills now use the complete track width: ratings render at 84%, 86%, 84%, and 88%, while review-volume bars remain proportional to the largest location count.

supervisorLogs.module: Mia Conversational Routing and Answer Surface Cleanup
supervisorLogs.change: Made Mia treat acknowledgements as small talk and removed visible evidence labels from the default answer surface
supervisorLogs.reason: The user wanted normal conversational replies for OK / got it / thanks / MIA messages, a cleaner user-facing answer without Short answer or Evidence used labels, and a friendlier thinking state and user label.
supervisorLogs.scope: Chat intent routing, user-facing answer formatting, evidence-card visibility, language detection, chat drawer expansion, responsive styles, backend and frontend fallback paths
supervisorLogs.result: Mia now routes short acknowledgements into thanks / small talk, replies in the detected input language, hides evidence by default unless the user explicitly asks for it, strips legacy Short answer / Evidence used labels before display, offers a larger expandable chat drawer with Enter-to-send behavior, and the rebuilt production dist now serves those changes in the browser.

supervisorLogs.module: Mia Composer and Customer Voice Badge Polish
supervisorLogs.change: Expanded Mia's question composer and centered Customer Voice priority badges
supervisorLogs.reason: The user reported that suggested Mia questions could not be read without scrolling inside the input, and that the High attention badge in Customer Voice looked visually off-center.
supervisorLogs.scope: Mia chat drawer width, textarea autosizing, suggested tag fill behavior, Customer Voice priority pill alignment, production dist
supervisorLogs.result: Mia now opens with a wider drawer and a taller autosizing textarea, while High attention badges keep their text centered inside the red priority pill.

supervisorLogs.change: Changed Mia to open collapsed by default and replaced long suggested questions with compact focus tags
supervisorLogs.reason: The user wanted the Q&A system to stay out of the way when the dashboard opens, and wanted only a few keyword prompts at the bottom instead of expanded long suggested questions.
supervisorLogs.scope: Mia chat launcher, focus tag prompts, chat drawer prompt styling, Update Log, production dist
supervisorLogs.result: The dashboard now opens with only the Ask Mia launcher visible; opening Mia shows compact tags for App risk, Route priority, Dover-Calais, Competitors, Marketing actions, and Evidence gaps, each still mapping to a useful report question.

supervisorLogs.module: Final 8766 UI QA and App Review Alignment
supervisorLogs.change: Completed the final source-level UI polish and live browser QA on the restored 8766 dashboard
supervisorLogs.reason: The first polish pass fixed the major regressions, but live screenshots still showed App Reviews platform text being squeezed and source logo sizing needed one more stable pass.
supervisorLogs.scope: App Reviews top-row alignment, source logo dimensions and spacing, competitor filter width, route-focus regression check, live 8766 smoke validation
supervisorLogs.result: App Reviews now keeps each platform card in one row with the logo and rating aligned at the top, Main data sources use compact 24x20 marks with a 12px title gap, Competitors keeps a 220px filter with an 8-column sticky benchmark table, and Overview route focus remains stable without the old ui-restore layer.

supervisorLogs.module: Dashboard UI Polish and Route Focus Stability
supervisorLogs.change: Rebuilt the React dashboard with route-focus stability fixes, priority ordering, tighter source/app layouts, and a shorter competitor filter
supervisorLogs.reason: The user reported that Overview route focus could blank the page, Customer Voice was not visually strong enough, Recommendations needed urgent-priority ordering, App Reviews had too much empty space, Main data source logos were cramped against text, and the Competitors filter input was too long.
supervisorLogs.scope: Overview route focus behavior, Main data sources spacing, Customer Voice priority ordering and card layout, App Reviews compact store cards, Recommendations priority sort, Competitors filter width, Vite production dist
supervisorLogs.result: The production dist now loads the rebuilt React bundle without the old ui-restore DOM mutation layer, route focus changes no longer blank the page, high-priority recommendations appear first, Customer Voice starts with high-attention signals, app ratings sit with store logos, and the competitor filter is compact.

supervisorLogs.change: Tightened the restored DFDS UI after live browser QA showed remaining navigation borders, oversized source logos, and weak benchmark sticky-row visibility
supervisorLogs.reason: The user confirmed that the sidebar still looked underlined, Trustpilot-style source icons still looked too large, and the competitor table controls and frozen DFDS row were not clear enough in the live 8766 page.
supervisorLogs.scope: Sidebar navigation border styling, Main data sources logo sizing and spacing, App Reviews store logo sizing, Ferry benchmark table scroll height, sticky header, sticky DFDS baseline row, live dist restore layer, cache-busting version
supervisorLogs.result: The live 8766 page now removes the nav border lines, reduces source logos to compact report-scale marks, makes App store logos smaller, and strengthens the benchmark table's filter/sort and frozen baseline presentation.

supervisorLogs.change: Restored the approved DFDS report-style UI patterns after the React route split changed several dashboard sections
supervisorLogs.reason: The user reported that the live 8766 frontend no longer matched the previously approved UI: All signals looked different, source logos were too large or cramped, the two app store cards were no longer aligned, the competitor benchmark missed filter and DFDS sticky baseline behavior, and sidebar links showed underlines.
supervisorLogs.scope: Overview route lens, Main data sources card spacing and logos, Customer temperature bar, App Reviews store cards, Ferry benchmark table filter/sort and DFDS sticky first row, sidebar navigation styling, cache-busting versions
supervisorLogs.result: The formal React source and live dist restore layer now preserve the earlier DFDS annual-report-inspired dashboard behavior while keeping the URL-based route shell.

supervisorLogs.change: Replaced the report shell with URL-based React subroutes for the major DFDS report sections
supervisorLogs.reason: The user asked for the Overview, Customer Voice, App Reviews, Competitors, Recommendations, Survey CSV, Update Log, Data Basis, and Review Console views to become separate subroutes instead of page-level tabs.
supervisorLogs.scope: React shell, route components, URL navigation, SPA fallback, cache-busting versioning
supervisorLogs.result: The dashboard now has route-owned sections with dedicated route components, and the browser can open each report page by path.

supervisorLogs.change: Attached the live /api/chat response flow to the validation harness
supervisorLogs.reason: Every real Mia reply should generate a review item automatically so the Review Console can catch regressions in route detection, small-talk routing, source labeling, and language handling without waiting for manual test runs.
supervisorLogs.scope: server.py /api/chat flow, validation harness invocation, validation metadata on chat responses, daily logs
supervisorLogs.result: Each successful chat turn now produces a validation run and review item alongside the normal answer, and the response includes validation metadata for internal inspection.

supervisorLogs.change: Added a deterministic validation agent and backend review-run endpoint
supervisorLogs.reason: The internal review console needs real validation items, not only seeded examples, so agent outputs can be checked for route drift, source overclaiming, evidence leakage, and language mismatch before publish.
supervisorLogs.scope: Validation agent, PostgreSQL review persistence helper, /api/review-runs/validate-chat, sample validation cases, unit tests, cache-busting versions, daily logs
supervisorLogs.result: The project can now run a validation batch from JSON or HTTP, produce review items, and write them to review_runs / review_items when PostgreSQL is connected.

supervisorLogs.change: Split Mia chat into vertical report questions and smalltalk bridge replies
supervisorLogs.reason: The user wanted the RAG path to separate serious DFDS report questions from light prompts, so smalltalk can answer briefly and then guide the manager back to the vertical report flow.
supervisorLogs.scope: Backend chat mode routing, frontend chat routing, live API payloads, response guidelines, daily logs, cache-busting versions
supervisorLogs.result: Report questions now run through the vertical retrieval path, while greetings, thanks, weather, and other light prompts use the smalltalk route for a short answer and a bridge back to the DFDS report.

supervisorLogs.change: Added a standalone internal review page for validation and reflection supervision
supervisorLogs.reason: The team needs a practical harness to inspect evidence chains, source limitations, RAG behavior, Mia guardrails, and release hygiene before new agent outputs are surfaced in the dashboard.
supervisorLogs.scope: Review Console navigation, seeded log-derived review records, review queue, detail panel, evidence chain, backend review schema and API, cache-busting versions
supervisorLogs.result: Internal reviewers can inspect seeded supervision items from the July 16-21 project logs and use the console as the first operational review workspace.

supervisorLogs.change: Removed the sidebar data collection snapshot card
supervisorLogs.reason: The user asked to remove the lower-left block showing Data collection, Public snapshot, and Collected July 16, 2026.
supervisorLogs.scope: Sidebar, stylesheet cleanup, cache-busting versions, Update Log
supervisorLogs.result: The sidebar now keeps only the DFDS brand area and main navigation, with no data snapshot card or unused collection-status styling.

supervisorLogs.change: Rewrote the page-opening Quick read blocks in more natural, plain business English
supervisorLogs.reason: The user felt the previous page summaries were still too abstract and wanted wording that sounds easier, more conversational, and clearer for non-technical stakeholders.
supervisorLogs.scope: Overview, Customer Voice, App Reviews, Competitors, Recommendations, Survey CSV, Update Log, Data Basis, cache-busting versions
supervisorLogs.result: Each page now starts with shorter, more direct guidance about what to look at first, what question the page answers, and how a manager can use it.

supervisorLogs.change: Rewrote the page summary blocks in simpler, more conversational English
supervisorLogs.reason: The user wanted each page summary to sound less abstract and easier for a business stakeholder to understand at a glance.
supervisorLogs.scope: Overview, Customer Voice, App Reviews, Competitors, Recommendations, Survey CSV, Update Log, Data Basis, cache-busting versions
supervisorLogs.result: Each page now starts with a plain-language Quick read that explains what the page is for, what to check first, and how to use it.

supervisorLogs.change: Extended evidence summaries and backend fallback evidence responses to all supported detected languages
supervisorLogs.reason: The user clarified that the same-language rule must apply to every language, not only Chinese; for example, Danish questions should receive Danish evidence summaries.
supervisorLogs.scope: Frontend evidence formatting, backend evidence-only fallback, multilingual language detection, cache-busting versions, daily logs
supervisorLogs.result: Mia now keeps local evidence summaries in the detected input language for Danish, German, French, Spanish, Japanese, Korean, Chinese, and English instead of mixing English evidence into non-English answers.

supervisorLogs.change: Localized Chinese evidence bullets and detected route names from the user's question
supervisorLogs.reason: The user asked in Chinese about Dover-Calais, but Mia returned Chinese wrapper text with English evidence bullets and kept the route focus as All signals.
supervisorLogs.scope: Local chat evidence formatting, route detection from message text, cache-busting versions, daily logs
supervisorLogs.result: Chinese questions now receive Chinese evidence summaries, and route mentions such as Dover-Calais influence the evidence focus even if the page dropdown remains All signals.

supervisorLogs.change: Expanded Mia's small-talk handling into dedicated greeting, identity, capability, wellbeing, thanks, apology, goodbye, joke, and confusion intents
supervisorLogs.reason: The user asked to add all common small talk so Mia behaves more like a mature commercial chatbot rather than a narrow report search box.
supervisorLogs.scope: Chat assistant intent routing, backend bridge replies, conversation guidelines, cache versioning, daily logs
supervisorLogs.result: Mia now answers common conversational prompts with short same-language replies and only bridges back to the DFDS report when that feels appropriate.

supervisorLogs.change: Added a second non-report intent guard before live chat calls and expanded greeting detection for messages like Mia hello

supervisorLogs.change: Added explicit small-talk, weather, and off-topic intent routing before evidence retrieval

supervisorLogs.scope: Conversation guidelines, chat intent classification, local fallback, backend bridge reply, cache versioning
supervisorLogs.result: Weather, greetings, and unrelated messages now receive a friendly same-language bridge back to the DFDS report instead of empty or mismatched evidence cards.

supervisorLogs.change: Made Mia answer greetings and out-of-report messages with a friendly bridge back to the DFDS report
supervisorLogs.reason: The user wanted the assistant to behave more like a mature chatbot that can handle unrelated chatter gracefully instead of dumping an empty evidence fallback.

supervisorLogs.reason: The user wanted the assistant to feel more natural and human, without a translation wrapper, and to answer in the language the manager actually used.

supervisorLogs.result: The assistant now introduces itself as Mia, shows no English/Translation wrappers, and returns Chinese, English, or other supported language responses directly in that same language.

supervisorLogs.change: Simplified the collapsed assistant launcher and replaced the text close button with an × icon
supervisorLogs.reason: The user wanted the chat assistant to feel closer to mature business chatbot patterns, with less visible copy and a more familiar close control.
supervisorLogs.scope: Floating chat launcher, chat drawer header, assistant note, initial assistant message, frontend cache versioning

recommendations.title: Build a disruption recovery message system for delay-heavy routes
recommendations.expectedImprovement: Customers know what is happening during delays and feel less ignored.
recommendations.reasoning: Delay complaints usually get worse when customers do not know what to expect. DFDS should send clear messages before the trip, during the delay, and after the crossing.
recommendations.evidence: Trustpilot negative themes, Dover delay reporting, Newhaven-Dieppe incident reporting.

recommendations.title: Separate Jersey and Channel Islands reporting from the all-company average
recommendations.expectedImprovement: DFDS can spot local trust problems earlier.
recommendations.reasoning: Jersey feedback has its own issues. If it is mixed into the total DFDS score, local problems may be missed until they become bigger.
recommendations.evidence: Public reporting on Jersey service, freight pricing, and disruption concerns.

recommendations.title: Turn staff friendliness into a proof-backed marketing asset
recommendations.expectedImprovement: DFDS can use a real customer strength in campaigns.
recommendations.reasoning: Many positive reviews mention helpful staff. This can support marketing messages, especially when DFDS also stays honest about delays and boarding issues.

recommendations.title: Audit the onboard promise around cabins, food, and boarding comfort
recommendations.expectedImprovement: Customers get a trip experience closer to what marketing promises.
recommendations.reasoning: Some complaints mention cabins, food, and boarding comfort. DFDS should check whether campaign messages match what passengers actually experience.

recommendations.title: Fix DFDS Passenger app authentication and booking retrieval before promoting mobile self-service
recommendations.expectedImprovement: Fewer customers lose confidence before they travel.
recommendations.reasoning: Recent app reviews mention login loops, missing bookings, and access errors. These are basic travel tasks, so they should work reliably before DFDS promotes the app heavily.
recommendations.evidence: Apple App Store GB review feed for DFDS - Passenger; Google Play GB rating details for com.dfds.pax.

recommendations.title: Add route-level mobile feature messaging
recommendations.expectedImprovement: Customers know which app features work on their route.
recommendations.reasoning: One Apple review says mobile check-in was not available for Newcastle to IJmuiden. The app should explain this before customers try to use it.
recommendations.evidence: Apple App Store GB review dated 2026-06-23.

recommendations.title: Use Google location strengths as route-level proof points
recommendations.expectedImprovement: Campaign claims feel more believable because they match public reviews.
recommendations.reasoning: Google location reviews show different strengths by route. Dover-Calais has terminal and staff signals, Newhaven has check-in and crossing signals, and Newcastle has onboard experience signals.
recommendations.evidence: Public Google location profiles for DFDS Calais, Dover, Newhaven, and Newcastle.

actarSlices.analysis: This group behaves like a practical transport audience that needs reliable vehicle-first planning.
actarSlices.recommendation: Prioritize boarding clarity, vehicle booking reassurance, ticket-rule clarity, and disruption timing.

actarSlices.triggerSignal: 137 synthetic trips; 86.9% cabin share; average order value 369.88.
actarSlices.analysis: Family travelers combine vehicle needs with comfort and planning needs.
actarSlices.recommendation: Prioritize family-package messaging, car guidance, school-holiday timing, and flexible-ticket content.

actarSlices.triggerSignal: 75 synthetic trips; 100.0% cabin share; average order value 501.39.
actarSlices.analysis: This group indexes toward premium cabins, comfort, lounge and overnight experience.
actarSlices.recommendation: Prioritize premium cabin proof points, onboard experience, meal bundles, and mini-cruise upgrades.

actarSlices.triggerSignal: 76 synthetic trips; 100.0% cabin share; average order value 425.85.
actarSlices.analysis: This is a leisure audience that responds to low-friction, confidence-building mini-cruise packaging.
actarSlices.recommendation: Prioritize easy itinerary planning, cabin comfort, assisted booking options, and calm onboarding messages.

itDataFlowSummary.title: IT Data Flow

pipelineStages.label: Upload
pipelineStages.detail: Accept the latest txt, pdf, or Word files and keep the original filename.

pipelineStages.label: Validate
pipelineStages.detail: Verify file type, recency, route hints, and source version before processing.

pipelineStages.label: Clean
pipelineStages.detail: Extract text, standardize dates and language, and remove obvious duplicates.

pipelineStages.label: Model
pipelineStages.detail: Map the batch into source, route, passenger, and memory dimensions.

pipelineStages.label: Serve
pipelineStages.detail: Expose the cleaned batch to dashboard views, Mia, and exportable summaries.

monitoring.label: File queue
monitoring.detail: Tracks batch size, file mix, and the most recent upload time.

monitoring.label: Version watch
monitoring.detail: Shows source versions, processing state, and batch lineage.

monitoring.label: Inferred dimensions
monitoring.detail: The guessed dimensions the agent uses before data reaches Mia.

monitoring.label: Agent reliability
monitoring.detail: Current confidence for extraction, mapping, and synthesis.

governanceChecks: Every file upload keeps original filename and source version.
Visible fields stay visible in Excel; inferred fields stay inside the model.
Human feedback can override weak batch inference before Mia reuses it.

sourceVersions.note: Trustpilot, Google Reviews, app stores, Reddit, and public source notes.
Synthetic star schema used by the Passenger Profile sub-agent.
Daily product changes and release notes stay aligned with the UI.
Future survey files will be versioned by upload date and schema.
Upload, processing, and memory surfaces stay aligned with the active page.

agentReliability.detail: Reads txt, pdf, and Word uploads into one clean text stream.
Infers route, source, and schema dimensions from the batch.
Turns the batch into a compact preview for the right rail.
Uses the shared context to answer in the current report language.

humanFeedback.label: Show upload preview first
humanFeedback.detail: Keep filename, file type, and batch size visible before the AI summary.

humanFeedback.label: Surface source version
humanFeedback.detail: Version tracking should be visible beside processing state.

humanFeedback.label: Expose inferred dimensions
humanFeedback.detail: When confidence drops, show the guessed dimensions explicitly.

batchPreview: New uploads keep original text, detected language, and version metadata.
Rows can be sliced into source, route, and memory dimensions before they reach Mia.
The preview should sit close to the upload form so the operator can sanity-check the batch.

memoryArchitectureSummary.title: Platform memory architecture

layers.scope: Recent turns, active route, selected files, open filters, and temporary UI state.
layers.purpose: Keep the current conversation and page context in view.

layers.storage: session state + batch metadata + feedback queue
layers.scope: Open upload batches, current dataset versions, active passenger-profile slices, and validation notes.
layers.purpose: Keep the active workstream coherent while the operator is still working.

layers.scope: Durable product rules, reusable analysis patterns, validated insights, and shared platform conventions.
layers.purpose: Reuse stable knowledge across sessions and product surfaces.

rules: Only long-term memory should store durable decisions.
Short-term memory should stay local to the current session or page.
Medium-term memory should decay once a batch or project slice closes.
Mia should cite evidence and memory separately when she answers a question.
Platform memory should support overview, passenger profile, survey, data basis, IT flow, and chatbot answers together.
